subject.title: [RFC] Multi-Agent Collaboration Enhancement: Capability Profiling + Shared Blackboard + Layered Memory + Token Cost Governance

question: Should OpenClaw pursue this RFC as a core roadmap direction, a plugin/ClawHub experimentation track, or defer/reject the heavy orchestration stack?
rationale: The RFC crosses core agent runtime, persistent storage, config, plugin API, privacy, and security boundaries; automation cannot choose that architecture from source evidence alone.

options.title: Keep as umbrella and split tracks
options.body: Leave this issue open as the canonical RFC while maintainers approve smaller design issues for capability evidence, blackboard/memory boundaries, and budget enforcement before code lands.

options.title: Route to plugin-first experiments
options.body: Ask contributors to prototype most collaboration behavior through plugins or ClawHub packages and bring back only missing core APIs.

options.title: Defer heavy orchestration
options.body: Close or freeze the RFC until there is maintainer demand for a core collaboration layer beyond current subagents and agent-to-agent tools.

recommendation.title: Keep as umbrella and split tracks
recommendation.body: Leave this issue open as the canonical RFC while maintainers approve smaller design issues for capability evidence, blackboard/memory boundaries, and budget enforcement before code lands.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest current-main history signal for the relevant agent/runtime and usage surfaces points to vincentkoc.
